confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web searches of aggregated cost-of-living data (MyLifeElsewhere, updated March 2026; ExpatExchange; Nomad Watch) and some bar and travel-guide listings. Sources agree closely: an inexpensive meal is about $2.50-$5, a three-course mid-range meal for two is $15-$30, local draft beer is $0.50-$2 and a cappuccino is $1.50-$2.50. I set the meal and beer anchors a little above the lowest figures to reflect tourist-area prices. Cocktail and wine figures are less certain. Most came from undated, venue-level or older listings: cocktails run about $3-$8 and house wine about $4-$5 a glass. I did not find a verified current Pub Street menu. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or live listings. July is low/green season in Siem Reap, so room rates for that window are likely at the softer end. Siem Reap prices are usually quoted in USD, so conversion risk is low. The FX value is the latest RBA observation available on the generation date (18 Nov 2026), not a July 2026 rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are based on Siem Reap data, cross-checked against Phnom Penh and other low-cost SEA tourist hubs such as Luang Prabang and Hoi An. These places have similar backpacker and mid-range tourism and a dense, competitive supply of budget hostels and guesthouses.
